title: OverSire daemon
description: The HTTP API of the oversire daemon on a machine, and the group of the machines of one user. Events use provider-event.json (kind session), the home store uses store.json and work orders use work-order.json.

MachineName.description: The daemon name (config name, default the host name). Unique in a group.

SessionReason.description: Why the session waits or stopped. monitoring: the session works, but only a background shell runs.

DaemonSession.description: One agent session on the machine, merged from all sources.

id.description: Stable on the machine. Orca: the pane key <tabId>:<leafId>. CLI: cli:<harness session id>. oversire runtime: the session id s-….

runtime.description: orca, oversire or cli (a harness outside a runtime). Open set.

harness.description: An agent-wire or AgentBinder harness name, for example claude or codex.

workspace.description: The Orca worktreeId, or the oversire workspace id.

cwd.description: The working folder of the agent.

question.description: The id of the open DaemonQuestion of the session.

stateSince.description: The start of the current state.

updatedAt.description: The last change of any field.

EventsPage.description: The answer of GET /v1/events?after=<seq>, on the cloud hub and on a daemon. The app reads it as CloudEventsPage.

next.description: The after value of the next call.

truncated.description: The log lost events after the after value. The reader does a full read.

HookEnv.description: The environment of the agent process. The oversire hook command sends it with each hook call.

ppid.description: The parent process id of the hook command.

oversireSession.description: The session id of the oversire runtime (s-…).

HarnessHooks.description: The hook state of one harness on the machine. untrusted: Codex did not approve the hooks yet.

DaemonInfo.description: The answer of GET /v1/whoami on a daemon. device is set only on a call with a credential. group is absent before the machine has a group.

home.description: The home machine of the group.

device.description: The device id of the credential of the call.

addrs.description: The addresses that other members dial, for example Tailscale addresses.

version.description: The CLI version of the member. Each member writes its own entry.

UpdateStatus.description: The last self-update check of a daemon. Absent before the first check, and on a dev build.

latest.description: The version of the latest release.

installed.description: The version that the check installed. The daemon restarts with it.

error.description: Why the check or the install failed, and what to do.

DeviceKind.description: daemon: a machine of the group. app: an app on a machine without a daemon.

issuedBy.description: The member that issued the credential.

Group.description: The My machines group. It never holds the secret. Only a JoinResult holds it.

home.description: The member that keeps the home store.

cloud.description: The cloud hub of the group, when the group uses one.

GroupInvite.description: A join code that a member made.

via.description: The member that made the code.

JoinRequest.description: The body of POST /v1/group/join and POST /v1/group/requests. code is absent for a request that waits for approval.

JoinPending.description: The answer of a join request that waits for approval. Both sides show confirm.

DeviceCredential.description: The token is opaque to clients.

JoinResult.description: The answer of an accepted join. Only a result for kind daemon holds the secret.

DaemonQuestionItem.description: The same shape as RunnerQuestionItem (work-order.json), plus the kind approve. An approve item has the options Allow and Deny.

DaemonQuestion.description: One open pause of a session. The fields match SessionQuestion of the app.

id.description: Stable for one pause: form:<tool_use_id>, form:<session>:<page hash>, turn:<session>:<stateSince ms> or wait:<session>:<stateSince ms>.

via.description: The same values as SessionQuestion.Via. askReply: a blocking ask of an Enhance worker.

answerable.description: False for waiting, and for a session with no terminal.

source.description: Where the items came from. mail: an ask of a supervised worker.

DaemonAnswerResult.description: The answer of POST /v1/questions/{id}/answer. The body of the call is a RunnerAnswer (work-order.json).

code.description: With error. Open set, for example form_changed.

message.description: With error. Text for the user.

SessionAsk.description: The body of POST /v1/sessions/{id}/ask (Member). The daemon sends the text to the session and waits for the end of the turn.

readOnly.description: Default true. The daemon adds one line to the text: Answer only. Do not change files.

SessionAskReply.description: The answer of POST /v1/sessions/{id}/ask. HTTP 200 has reply. HTTP 409 (a turn is active and the session takes no steering) and 504 (timeout) have error and screenTail.

reply.description: The last agent message of the turn.

screenTail.description: The last lines of the screen, when the runtime has a screen.

error.description: With 409 and 504. Open set: busy, timeout.

message.description: With error. Text for the user.

DaemonRuntime.description: One agent runtime on the machine. The daemon talks only to the runtimes of its own machine.

name.description: Text for the user, for example Orca.

installed.description: The daemon found the runtime program.

reachable.description: The runtime answered its last status call.

error.description: Why the runtime is not reachable. Text for the user.

capabilities.description: The same raw values as Capability of the app, for example sessionInput, reveal, hostFiles. sessionStream: GET /v1/sessions/{id}/stream works for the sessions of this runtime. Open set.

RuntimeStream.description: The state of the live session stream of a runtime. live: live bytes. pairing: the daemon connects to the runtime now. textOnly: the daemon reads the screen as text, reason tells why. POST /v1/runtimes/{id}/retry (Member) connects again and gives the DaemonRuntime. POST /v1/runtimes/{id}/pair (Member, body RuntimePair) keeps a pairing link and DELETE forgets it. Both give the DaemonRuntime. HTTP 400: the link did not pair. HTTP 501: the runtime takes no link.

reason.description: Text for the user, for example Orca 1.3.9 is older than 1.4.200.

pairable.description: The runtime takes a pairing link from the user.

paired.description: The daemon keeps a pairing link.

RuntimePair.description: The body of POST /v1/runtimes/{id}/pair (Member). The link holds a device token: do not log it.

link.description: For Orca: the runtime pairing link from Orca › Settings.

DaemonRepo.description: One repo that a runtime knows.

folder.description: A plain folder, not a git repo.

DaemonTerminal.description: One terminal of a workspace. A terminal can hold an agent session.

session.description: The DaemonSession id of the terminal (Orca: the pane key).

orphaned.description: The terminal has no live process.

DaemonWorkspace.description: One runtime workspace: an Orca card, a worktree of the oversire runtime.

id.description: The workspace id of the runtime (Orca worktreeId).

kind.description: worktree: a git worktree of its own. folder: a card on a shared folder. main: the main checkout of a repo.

DaemonWorkspacesPage.description: The answer of GET /v1/workspaces (Member). A runtime that does not answer is in errors, not in workspaces.

force.description: Remove a workspace with changes that are not committed.

runHooks.description: Run the archive hooks of the runtime.

WorkspaceRemoval.description: The answer of DELETE /v1/workspaces/{id}. HTTP 404: no runtime knows the workspace.

warning.description: A note of the runtime, for example a kept branch or a failed hook.

name.description: A plain file name. No folder, no .. and no leading dot.

WorkspaceFiles.description: The body of POST /v1/files (Member). The daemon writes the files into a new folder of its own and gives their full paths. The client cannot choose the folder. At most 20 files and 25 MB.

WorkspaceFilesResult.description: The answer of POST /v1/files. The paths are in the order of the files.

WorkerStart.description: The body of POST /v1/workers (Member). Start a supervised worker that reads the code and sends one result.

path.description: The folder that the worker works in.

agent.description: A harness name, for example claude.

Worker.description: The answer of POST /v1/workers. The daemon keeps the worker in its data folder: the worker survives a restart.

terminal.description: The terminal handle of the worker, for reveal.

WorkerState.description: The answer of GET /v1/workers/{id}. HTTP 404: the daemon does not know the worker.

state.description: done: the worker sent its result. ended: the worker stopped with no result.

outcome.description: With done. Open set, for example succeeded.

body.description: With done. The result text of the worker.

reason.description: With ended. The last state of the worker in the runtime.
